lines.japanese: ガード下でもらった数々の痛みを引きつれて、ひとり夜の街を歩いた。
lines.english: Carrying every ache I'd collected beneath the tracks, I walked the nighttime city alone.

lines.japanese: あのリンチまがいの輪をくぐり抜けた体に、深刻なダメージがなさそうなのは幸運だった。
lines.english: I was lucky. After fighting my way out of that mob beating, my body seemed to have taken no serious damage.

lines.japanese: しかし今日ばかりはタクシーを使おう。疲弊した頭でそう考えて、俺は大通りを目指した。
lines.english: I decided, through a haze of exhaustion, to take a cab tonight and headed for the main road.

lines.japanese: 喘ぐたびに白い息が紫色の空に昇ってゆく。もう日付の上では日曜だ。
lines.english: Each pant sent a white breath climbing into the violet sky. By the calendar, it was Sunday already.

lines.japanese: 朝、布団の中で目覚めるタカシは、体じゅうにできた色とりどりの痣を見つけてどう思うだろう。例によってグレタガルドでの名誉ある負傷と解釈して、聖騎士ホークの活躍を誇るのかもしれない。
lines.english: When Takashi woke under the covers that morning, what would he make of the many-colored bruises all over his body? As usual, perhaps he would take them for honorable wounds earned in Gretagard and boast of the Holy Knight Hawk's exploits.

lines.japanese: 最近は一日の中で、俺と鷲介とタカシ──三人の出てくる周期が安定してきて、小学生の組んだ夏休みの日程表ぐらいには規則的な毎日を過ごすことが出来るようになっていた。
lines.english: Lately, the cycle in which the three of us—me, Shusuke, and Takashi—appeared over the course of a day had settled down. Our lives had grown about as regular as a summer-vacation timetable drawn up by an elementary school kid.

lines.japanese: それは永すぎる年月と経験と修錬を積みかさねた成果だ。
lines.english: It was the fruit of far too many years, far too much experience, far too much discipline.

lines.japanese: 日中はタカシに学校へ通わせ、俺が夜のうちに金を稼ぎ、そのあいだを鷲介が繋ぐ。このシフトがなんとか形になったのは一、二年前のことだ。
lines.english: Takashi went to school by day, I earned money by night, and Shusuke bridged the hours between. It was only a year or two ago that we finally made the shift work.

lines.japanese: そりゃあ多少の不都合はあったけれど、それでもこの態勢なら、この三人ならずっと共存していける──そう思っていたのに。
lines.english: Sure, it came with inconveniences. Even so, under this arrangement, the three of us could go on coexisting forever—or so I had thought.

lines.japanese: ひとり増えた。
lines.english: Now there was one more.

lines.japanese: しかも非協力的な──それどころか、反社会的なやつだ。
lines.english: And he was uncooperative. Worse, he was antisocial.

lines.japanese: どうなるんだろう。
lines.english: What would become of us?

lines.japanese: 俺たちの均衡は崩れてしまうのか。
lines.english: Would our balance collapse?

lines.japanese: なあ。やっぱりおまえは俺たちに統合を勧めに来たのか？
lines.english: Hey. Did you come to urge us to integrate after all?

lines.japanese: 引きずる体がやけに重く感じられた。
lines.english: The body I dragged along felt strangely heavy.

lines.japanese: いつもの倍の時間をかけて──それだけの時間を不安な思索に費やして、俺は真夜中の花水木通りに出た。
lines.english: It took me twice as long as usual—and I spent every minute of it worrying—before I emerged onto Flowering Dogwood Street at midnight.

lines.japanese: 思わず目を凝らす。通りの先にチョコレート色の巨大な木箱が見えた。
lines.english: I squinted without meaning to. Farther down the street stood a gigantic chocolate-brown wooden box.

lines.japanese: 屋台だ。
lines.english: A food stall.

lines.japanese: 「あいつ……」
lines.english: “That guy...”

lines.japanese: いつもの場所にいつものラーメン屋が店を出している。俺はガードレールの向こうを走るタクシーに目もくれず、そのまま歩道を進んだ。
lines.english: The usual ramen stand was open in its usual place. I ignored the taxis running beyond the guardrail and kept down the sidewalk.

lines.japanese: 歩みは一歩一歩速くなる。近付くにつれ表情が緩む。暗い思いも疼く痛みも、俺はすべて忘れて走った。空きっ腹に堪えるあの温かな匂いが風のように鼻腔を撫でた。
lines.english: My steps quickened one by one. The closer I came, the more my face relaxed. I forgot every dark thought and throbbing pain and broke into a run. That warm smell, irresistible on an empty stomach, brushed my nose like a breeze.

lines.japanese: 「おまえら……」
lines.english: “You guys...”

lines.japanese: 白い湯気の向こうに呼びかける。喉から漏れたのは、張りのないひょろけた声だった。
lines.english: I called through the white steam. What leaked from my throat was a thin, unsteady voice.

lines.japanese: 俺はさらに近付き、腹の底から声を飛ばした。
lines.english: I came closer and sent the next call up from the pit of my stomach.

lines.japanese: 「おっさんラーメン一丁！　いちばん安いの！」
lines.english: “One ramen, old man! Cheapest thing you've got!”

lines.japanese: 真っ赤な暖簾が撥ねあげられ、カウンター席の女が振りかえる。
lines.english: The brilliant red curtain snapped upward, and the woman at the counter turned around.

lines.japanese: 「おうドラ、やっぱり来たな」
lines.english: “Hey, Drac. Knew you'd show.”

lines.japanese: 屋台の木枠の陰から、いかつい渋面を絆創膏と包帯で飾った大男が巨体を覗かせる。
lines.english: From behind the stall's wooden frame, a huge man leaned out, his forbidding scowl decorated with bandages and adhesive strips.

lines.japanese: 「ラーメン一丁まいど」
lines.english: “One ramen. Coming right up.”

lines.japanese: そして──
lines.english: And then—

lines.japanese: ──女の隣りに座っていた若草色のスーツ姿が、日焼けサロンで仕上げたサニーブラウンの二枚目ヅラに、映画スターみたいな白い歯を輝かせた。
lines.english: —the man in the pale-green suit beside her flashed movie-star teeth from a handsome, sunny-brown face perfected in a tanning salon.

lines.japanese: 「あれドラさん！　あっはっはっ、あんたまた仕事サボってこんなとこ……」
lines.english: “Hey, Drac! Ahahaha! Skipping work to hang around a place like—”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ！」
lines.english: “Shut up!”

lines.japanese: 俺はプラチナの言葉を遮ってカウンター席の真ん中に飛びこんだ。やつらは迷惑そうな苦言を並べたてながら笑顔で隙間を空けてくれる。
lines.english: I cut Platinum off and hurled myself into the middle seat at the counter. They made room for me with smiles, all the while piling on mock complaints.

lines.japanese: 「まー、こんな時間によく来たねえ」
lines.english: “Well, look at you showing up so late.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　そりゃ来るだろ！　なぁ！」
lines.english: “Huh? Of course I came! Right?”

lines.japanese: 「痛っ！　ちょっ、なんで僕ひっぱたかれんすか、意味わかんないっすよ！」
lines.english: “Ow! Wait—why'd you slap me? What did I do?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ドラは俺に似て感情表現が不器用な男だからな」
lines.english: “Well, Drac is clumsy about expressing his emotions. Much like me.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえ！　最高だてめえら、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ！」
lines.english: “Shut up! You bastards are the best! I'll fucking kill you, asshole!”

lines.japanese: 森里は帰れる場所がないと言っていた。
lines.english: Morisato had said he had nowhere to go home to.

lines.japanese: しかし、俺にはまだ帰れる場所があった。
lines.english: But I still did.

lines.japanese: それはとても嬉しいことで、そんな当たり前のことに、俺は今ごろになって気付いた。
lines.english: That made me really happy, and only now did I realize something that obvious.

lines.japanese: だから俺は、ほんのちょっぴり目に真珠汁を溜めた。
lines.english: So the tiniest bit of pearl juice gathered in my eyes.

lines.japanese: まあ、べつに泣いたってほどじゃねえけどな。
lines.english: Not enough to call it crying or anything.
